name: – Nacho Sánchez Amor – § 57 – Am 6
title: REPORT on the 2025 Commission report on Türkiye
part_text: 57. Supports the decision taken by the EU component of the EU-Türkiye Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to postpone its 82nd meeting, scheduled to take place on 14 and 15 April 2025 in Ankara, in the aftermath of the detention and arrest of Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and others; retains the view that parliamentary dialogue remains a crucial part of EU-Türkiye relations and expresses the hope that the work of the JPC will resume soon when conditions allow; regrets the Turkish authorities’ decision not to invite the European Parliament to observe the presidential and parliamentary elections in May 2023 amid allegations of unfair treatment, noting that the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe were invited; expresses its hope that a European Parliament mission will be invited to observe any upcoming elections in the country and calls on the Commission to engage with relevant partners, notably the Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe and the Council of Europe, to create a robust and reinforced election monitoring mechanism for the next Turkish elections, scheduled for 2028, covering the whole electoral cycle, and to commit to using the findings of the resulting reinforced election monitoring programme to assess, and report back to Parliament on, whether it is still possible to continue to maintain the formal but frozen accession process for the country or whether this process has come to an end;
